blocks.text: `-p HOST:CONTAINER` creates a host-side forwarding rule, binding all interfaces unless you give an IP; EXPOSE is metadata only; container-to-container traffic never needs publishing.

rows: All EXPOSEd ports to random host ports

blocks.code:
services:
  db:
    ports: ["127.0.0.1:5433:5432"]      # host port 5433
  api:
    environment:
      DATABASE_URL: postgresql://app@db:5432/rag   # container port, not 5433

items: `-p 5432:5432` on a cloud VM exposes Postgres to the internet.
Using the host port between containers (`db:5433`) → connection refused.
"port is already allocated": another container (maybe another Compose project) or a host process holds it; check `docker ps`, `ss -ltnp`.

blocks.text: Q: "EXPOSE vs -p?" A: "EXPOSE only documents the port (and feeds -P); -p creates the host mapping, on 0.0.0.0 by default. Containers on the same network reach each other on the container port without any publishing, so databases shouldn't be published at all or only on 127.0.0.1."

items: -p binds 0.0.0.0 unless you add an IP.
